req_description (Final Language): Verify that accounts used to publish packages require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication, and that this requirement applies separately to each package
risk_if_absent: Maintainer account phished, malicious version published to millions

req_description (Final Language): Verify that no single credential can write to more than one repository, package, or service. Break broad-access credentials into smaller, single-purpose ones
risk_if_absent: One stolen token self-replicates across every package it can publish

req_description (Final Language): Verify that source code repository read access for all identities, including human users and programmatic identities such as service accounts, CI/CD tokens, and bot accounts, is scoped by team or project and is not granted organization-wide by default.
risk_if_absent: One compromised identity reads every repo in the org

req_description (Final Language): Verify that CI/CD workflow permissions default to read-only at the platform or organization level, and that write permissions are granted only per workflow with documented justification.
risk_if_absent: An over-privileged workflow token is abused to write/publish

req_description (Final Language): Verify that build, signing, and publish stages execute on systems that share no administrative accounts, no privileged credentials, and no credential store, so that compromise of one stage does not grant access to the next.
risk_if_absent: A single stage compromise cascades into full build-to-publish control

req_description (Final Language): Verify that developer tool installations, configuration files, and extension or add-on inventory are monitored for unauthorized changes, and that alerts are routed to a documented response process.
risk_if_absent: An approved extension trojanized after approval, or an unapproved tool added quietly, persists undetected on developer systems.

req_description (Final Language): Verify that runtime communication destinations of installed developer tool extensions and add-ons are governed by a destination allowlist or a documented destination policy with periodic review, and that communication with a destination outside the allowlist or policy triggers an alert.
risk_if_absent: A compromised extension exfiltrates credentials and AI-assistant configuration indefinitely because no control watches where developer tools connect.

req_description (Final Language): Verify that IDE extensions are limited to a centrally approved list, pinned to a specific version, and verified by checksum at install and update. Auto-update shall be disabled or allowed only through the same approval and verification process. Any extension outside the approved list, version drift, checksum mismatch, or auto-update path that bypasses these controls shall be considered a failure.
risk_if_absent: Malicious or auto-updated IDE extension runs with developer privileges

req_description (Final Language): Verify that developer toolchain execution is isolated from host operating system credentials, configuration files, and network resources through containerized development environments, sandboxed application profiles, or equivalent process-level isolation.
risk_if_absent: Any code execution inside the toolchain immediately yields host credentials, keys, and AI-assistant sessions.

req_description (Final Language): Verify that opening a cloned or downloaded repository in a developer tool cannot trigger automatic code execution, including workspace task auto-run, tool activation hooks, and container initialization, until the user has explicitly assigned trust to that workspace.
risk_if_absent: Cloning a repository and opening it in an IDE executes attacker code with no further interaction, the largest active campaign vector in the window.
attack_technique: workspace trust enforced before repo-open execution

req_description (Final Language): Verify that the pipeline enforces cryptographic verification of commit signatures against an approved signer list, and that commits failing verification are rejected.
risk_if_absent: Spoofed or unsigned commit accepted from a CLI or automated path

req_description (Final Language): Verify that local environment files are never used to store secrets in plain text. Use a secrets manager or encrypted storage instead
risk_if_absent: Infostealer reads plaintext creds from local env/config files

req_description (Final Language): Verify that scripts which run automatically during package installation, such as preinstall or postinstall hooks, are turned off by default. Only turn them on for packages that have been specifically reviewed and approved
risk_if_absent: Install-time script (or native-build file) executes attacker code

req_description (Final Language): Verify that new packages and package versions are screened for defined risk signals, including at minimum install scripts, very low maintainer count, very recent publication age, and no linked source repository, and that a minimum publish-age is enforced before trust in development or build environments. A package or version that does not pass screening or satisfy the minimum publish-age shall be considered a failure.
risk_if_absent: A freshly-published malicious version is installed before anyone notices

req_description (Final Language): Verify that a lockfile is integrity-checked against the manifest before a build consumes it, and that the build fails when a package source, version, or integrity hash differs from the recorded value.
risk_if_absent: Tampered lockfile silently redirects a dependency to a malicious source

req_description (Final Language): Verify that the number of third-party dependencies, and how many layers deep they go, is reviewed regularly and reduced where possible
risk_if_absent: Deep transitive dependency sprawl widens the attack surface

req_description (Final Language): Verify that a requested package name is screened against known-good internal and public names before first resolution, and that a near-match to an existing name, or a name never previously used in the organization, requires review before install.
risk_if_absent: A near-name or hallucinated package resolves and installs, delivering a stealer through simple name confusion.

req_description (Final Language): Verify that packages from public registries are consumed through a private registry proxy or mirror, and that direct installation from public registries is blocked in CI/CD environments.
risk_if_absent: Resolution falls back to a public index and pulls an attacker package

req_description (Final Language): Verify that build and CI/CD pipelines install dependencies using a command that installs exactly what's listed in the lockfile, instead of a command that can pull in newer versions on its own
risk_if_absent: A floating install pulls a newer, malicious version at build time

req_description (Final Language): Verify that text coming from outside the organization, such as a contributor's branch name, commit message, or pull request title, is never inserted directly into a command that the pipeline runs
risk_if_absent: Attacker-controlled input is interpolated into a pipeline command (injection)

req_description (Final Language): Verify that build and publish are two separate pipeline stages, with the built artifact held in between for review. No single pipeline run should be allowed to both build and publish without a check in between
risk_if_absent: A single compromised run builds and publishes a tampered artifact unchecked

req_description (Final Language): Verify that every change to a pipeline or workflow file is scanned by an automated tool before it's merged, checking for unsafe triggers, unescaped external input in commands, and permissions broader than needed
risk_if_absent: An unsafe trigger (e.g. pull_request_target) or over-broad permission is merged

req_description (Final Language): Verify that every container base image used in a build or CI step is pinned to a specific digest, not a tag that can change. If the digest doesn't match what's expected, the pipeline should fail
risk_if_absent: A mutable base-image tag is repointed to a malicious image

req_description (Final Language): Verify that CI/CD runners are ephemeral and destroyed after each job, or that persistent runners are re-imaged on a defined schedule and scanned for tampering before reuse.
risk_if_absent: A persistent runner retains attacker implants across jobs

req_description (Final Language): Verify that dependency installation and build execution occur in an isolated environment whose outbound network access is denied by default and permitted only to approved package sources and explicitly approved endpoints, so that code executing during install or build cannot download additional stages or send data to arbitrary destinations.
risk_if_absent: A payload that executes during install or build has unrestricted egress to download stages and exfiltrate credentials.

req_description (Final Language): Verify that secrets given to a shared or reusable pipeline are limited to the one job that needs them, instead of being automatically passed to every job in the chain
risk_if_absent: Secrets flow to every job in a reusable chain, widening exposure

req_description (Final Language): Verify that secrets are not shared across an entire organization or across all repositories. Each project should have its own credentials, scoped to only what that project needs
risk_if_absent: One leaked org-wide secret unlocks every repository

req_description (Final Language): Verify that when a publish workflow has both a short-lived OIDC credential and a static token configured, the static token is removed rather than left as a silent fallback
risk_if_absent: A silent static-token fallback beside OIDC is abused to publish

req_description (Final Language): Verify that security scanning tools are themselves checked for integrity before they run, so a compromised scanning tool can't falsely mark its own output as clean
risk_if_absent: A compromised scanner (the TeamPCP vector) passes itself as clean

req_description (Final Language): Verify that dependency installation and build steps in pipeline build environments run in an instrumented environment, and that a child process, script interpreter launch, or network connection that is not expected for the declared build triggers an alert.
risk_if_absent: Malicious code that executes during install or build, from any entry point including ones install-script controls do not cover, runs unobserved.

req_description (Final Language): Verify that every published artifact is automatically compared against the output of its release pipeline, including declared version, embedded build metadata, and content digest, and that any divergence triggers an alert and blocks promotion.
risk_if_absent: A tampered artifact published through a legitimate or breached trusted-publishing path ships because nothing compares what was published to what the pipeline built.

req_description (Final Language): Verify that build outputs include a signed provenance attestation that binds the artifact to its source, builder identity, and build parameters, and that downstream consumers validate this attestation before use.
risk_if_absent: No enforced artifact-to-source binding; a tampered artifact ships (Axios check-before-use failure)

req_description (Final Language): Verify that each pipeline stage checks the signature of any artifact it receives from the stage before it, against a known trust source. If that check fails, the pipeline run should fail too
risk_if_absent: An unverified/tampered artifact is passed between stages

req_description (Final Language): Verify that pinned commit references actually point to a commit that exists on a real branch, not an orphan or "shadow" commit that was never merged anywhere
risk_if_absent: A pin to a shadow/orphan commit hides malicious code

req_description (Final Language): Verify that CI/CD cache contents are signed or checksummed at write time, and that the verification key, signature, or checksum is stored in a separate trust boundary from the cache. Restored cache contents shall be verified against that value before use. A cache whose integrity value is stored with the cache, or that fails verification before use, shall be considered a failure.
risk_if_absent: Poisoned cache is restored and trusted in a later build

req_description (Final Language): Verify that build provenance attestations are validated not only for signature, but also for recorded builder identity and isolation state against an expected baseline. An attestation missing these fields or not matching the expected baseline shall be considered a failure.
risk_if_absent: A validly-signed attestation from a tampered build environment is trusted
attack_technique: valid signature but tampered build env

req_description (Final Language): Verify that a release tag or version reference cannot be quietly overwritten once it has been published
risk_if_absent: Release tags are force-pushed to malicious commits (the TeamPCP move)

req_description (Final Language): Verify that pinned external build steps or plugins use only pinned dependencies, evidenced by a recursive dependency manifest or vendored dependencies. Where full transitive pinning is not feasible, first-order dependencies shall be pinned and deeper transitive risk documented.
risk_if_absent: A pinned Action pulls an unpinned transitive dependency that is swapped

req_description (Final Language): Verify that signature and attestation checks for deployment cannot be bypassed except through a documented break-glass process that generates an immediate alert and requires post-incident review.
risk_if_absent: Verification is bypassed via a break-glass path and an unverified artifact ships

req_description (Final Language): Verify that the release stage refuses any credential carried over from the integrate stage or any earlier stage. Release actions should only work with credentials issued specifically for release
risk_if_absent: An earlier-stage credential is reused to perform a release

req_description (Final Language): Verify that where a single publishing identity is authorized to release more than one package that identity cannot release new versions of multiple packages in rapid succession without an additional approval.
risk_if_absent: One stolen publishing credential republishes across every reachable package in minutes; detection alone cannot outpace machine-speed propagation.
attack_technique: publish rate and blast-radius bound; release-manifest gate

req_description (Final Language): Verify that every software component running in production can be traced to a current, pinned SBOM generated by the build pipeline and validated before deployment, confirming nothing was installed outside the approved build process.
risk_if_absent: A component installed outside the normal build reaches production untraced

req_description (Final Language): Verify that outbound network traffic from CI/CD runners is monitored, and that an alert fires when a connection goes to an unexpected or unauthorized destination
risk_if_absent: C2/exfiltration egress from a runner goes unnoticed

req_description (Final Language): Verify that only the specific processes that need it are allowed to query internal cloud metadata endpoints from a build agent, and that any other process doing so triggers an alert
risk_if_absent: A build process pulls cloud metadata/IMDS credentials

req_description (Final Language): Verify that one process reading another process's memory on a build agent is treated as abnormal and triggers an alert
risk_if_absent: A runner-memory dump harvests secrets (tj-actions pattern) undetected

req_description (Final Language): Verify that publishing a new package version from an automated pipeline always sends a notification, and that any publish the team didn't expect gets investigated before it's trusted
risk_if_absent: An unexpected or mass republish (worm behaviour) goes uninvestigated

req_description (Final Language): Verify that any workload appearing in a shared or system-level part of a runtime cluster is checked against an approved list, so anything deployed with stolen pipeline credentials gets caught quickly
risk_if_absent: A workload deployed with stolen pipeline credentials runs unnoticed

req_description (Final Language): Verify that changes to CI/CD pipeline definitions, workflow files, and build configurations generate alerts and are logged with the identity of the actor who made the change.
risk_if_absent: A pipeline-as-code modification (attacker persistence) is not alerted

req_description (Final Language): Verify that developer endpoints generate alerts when an installed extension, add-on, or tool bundle produces anomalous behaviour, including network egress from test runners or build tools, reads of credential files outside the user session context, or process activity inconsistent with the approved purpose of the tool.
risk_if_absent: Malicious code running inside an approved developer tool context harvests credentials on the workstation with nothing watching for it.
attack_technique: endpoint behavioural anomaly detection (pairs with P1)

req_description (Final Language): Verify that when a credential is rotated because of an incident, the compromised credential is revoked before the replacement is activated, and within a defined SLO.
risk_if_absent: A compromised credential stays valid during rotation and is abused
